age.evidence: Adult female CRF1:GFP mice (n=90, 2-8 months, 18-30 g)

sex.evidence: Adult female CRF1:GFP mice (n=90, 2-8 months, 18-30 g)

dosing.evidence: Mice were subcutaneously injected with 2 ml/kg of either 2 mg/kg psilocin or vehicle (2% glacial acetic acid in 0.9% saline).

group_housing.evidence: Mice in the ethanol drinking cohorts (n=60) were individually housed for two-bottle choice (2BC) drinking.

day_night_flipped.evidence: housed in a temperature- and humidity-controlled 12 h reverse light/dark (7 A.M. lights off) facility

assays.assay_description: Individually housed mice given 2 h home-cage access (Mon-Fri) to 20% ethanol and water bottles; ethanol and water intake measured at 1 h and 2 h timepoints across baseline, treatment, and follow-up sessions. Some mice received CIE vapor exposure intervening between drinking weeks (CIE-2BC vs AIR-2BC).

application_type.evidence: Mice were subcutaneously injected with 2 ml/kg of either 2 mg/kg psilocin or vehicle

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were individually housed for at least 5 d prior to the start of drinking for habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were individually housed for two-bottle choice (2BC) drinking

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum food (RMH-3000) and water access

water_restriction.evidence: ad libitum food (RMH-3000) and water access; two bottles, one containing 20% ethanol solution and one containing water

time_to_assay.evidence: Psilocin decreased ethanol consumption in the session immediately following injection

sample_size.evidence: Vehicle: n=10; Psilocin: n=10 (Fig 1). AIR: n=10; CIE: n=10 (Fig 2).

outcomes.summary: Acute 2 mg/kg psilocin (s.c.) reduced 1 h and 2 h ethanol intake in the drinking session immediately following injection in both CIE-exposed and air-exposed female mice. The effect was acute and did not persist in subsequent sessions; water intake was largely unchanged (slight increase in 2nd hour in one cohort).
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA, Fig 1D treatment p=0.0003, F(1,18)=19.33; Fig 1F treatment×time p=0.0081, multiple comparisons Veh vs Psi p=0.0072; Fig 2F CIE treatment p=0.0313, F(1,15)=5.643; Fig 2G AIR treatment p=0.0013, F(1,18)=14.34
outcomes.evidence: Psilocin decreased ethanol consumption in the session immediately following injection with a main effect of treatment and time (two-way ANOVA, treatment: ***p=0.0003, F(1,18)=19.33)

B1_num_measures.evidence: 1 h ethanol intake, 2 h ethanol intake, 1 h water intake, 2 h water intake; also ethanol preference reported in supplementary

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: One hour intake was recorded to compare any immediate consumption to the total 2 h duration and determine whether mice were front-loading

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no analysis of bout sequences or transitions reported

B4_ethological.evidence: only ethanol/water intake volumes were quantified; no natural behavioural acts scored

B5_social.evidence: Mice were individually housed for two-bottle choice (2BC) drinking

B6_cognitive.evidence: voluntary drinking; no learning task component

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Alcohol intake was determined by visual inspection of ethanol volume according to meniscus on serological pipettes

E1_environment_type.evidence: Mice were individually housed for two-bottle choice (2BC) drinking

E2_shelter.evidence: no shelter mentioned in home cage

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard home-cage drinking implies bedding present

E6_spatial.evidence: single home cage with two bottles, no internal partitions

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were individually housed for two-bottle choice (2BC) drinking

E8_food_water.evidence: two bottles, one containing 20% ethanol solution and one containing water; ad libitum food

D1_continuity.evidence: Mice underwent 2 weeks of baseline 2BC drinking followed by alternating 2BC weeks and CIE weeks for another 4 weeks; recordings of 5 sessions following injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: Mice were given 2 h access (Mon-Fri) to two bottles

D3_recording_days.evidence: 2 weeks of baseline 2BC drinking (Mon-Fri) plus alternating drinking weeks for 4 more weeks plus 5 post-injection sessions

D4_baseline.evidence: Mice underwent 2 weeks of baseline 2BC drinking

D5_followup.evidence: drinking measured for 5 sessions following injection

D6_circadian.evidence: 2 h access sessions; no single session ≥6 h

assays.assay_description: 41 cm × 41 cm × 30 cm open-field chamber (Versa Max, AccuScan) with infrared photo-beam tracking. 10 min free-movement session measuring total distance, distance in centre, thigmotaxis, distance per minute, and time spent in centre.

application_type.evidence: Mice were subcutaneously injected with either vehicle or psilocin (2 mg/kg) before habituating in the room with the machines on for 90 min

setup_habituation.evidence: habituating in the room with the machines on for 90 min — room habituation only, not apparatus habituation

setup_restrain.evidence: the mice were placed into the boxes and allowed to move freely for 10 min

food_restriction.evidence: open field chamber; no food in apparatus

water_restriction.evidence: open field chamber; no water in apparatus

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were subcutaneously injected with either vehicle or psilocin (2 mg/kg) before habituating in the room with the machines on for 90 min. Once habituation was complete, the mice were placed into the boxes

sample_size.evidence: locomotor cohort (n=20)... Vehicle: n=10; Psilocin: n=10

outcomes.summary: Acute 2 mg/kg psilocin did not alter total distance traveled, distance traveled per minute, or time spent in centre compared with vehicle, indicating no sedation, hyperlocomotion, or anxiety-like effect at this dose.
outcomes.statistics: Unpaired t test: total distance p=0.5354, t=0.6318, df=18; two-way ANOVA distance by minute p=0.1170, F(9,162)=1.608; centre time t test p=0.6409, t=0.4744, df=18
outcomes.evidence: we measured locomotion and found no difference in total distance traveled... distance traveled by minute... or time spent in center between vehicle and psilocin

B1_num_measures.evidence: multiple values were measured including total distance traveled in center, total distance traveled, thigmotaxis, and time course data of locomotion

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Distance traveled by minute during locomotor testing

B7_automated_classification.evidence: x-y-z spatial positioning was recorded through three sets of infrared photo beams — beam-break position tracking

E1_environment_type.evidence: computer-controlled open field chamber (41 cm × 41 cm × 30 cm; Versa Max, AccuScan Instruments)

E6_spatial.evidence: open field chamber - single open arena

E7_social_context.evidence: mice were placed into the boxes individually

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to move freely for 10 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to move freely for 10 min

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline recording in same apparatus reported

judge_notes: Two assays identified consistently across candidates: Two-Bottle Choice Drinking and Open Field (locomotor) Test. All candidates agreed on these.
Excluded non-behavioural endpoints: immunohistochemistry/c-Fos quantification and corticosterone ELISA are not behavioural assays.

group_housing scored 'no' at study level because mice in drinking cohorts (60/90) were individually housed during testing; the locomotor/naive cohort housing differed but the dominant testing condition for behavioural assays involved single housing — note that locomotor cohort was group housed prior to treatment.
setup_habituation for OFT scored 'no': only room habituation (90 min in testing room) was described, not exposure to the apparatus itself.

E3 bedding for 2BC scored 'Yes' because the test is conducted in the animal's home cage which by default contains bedding (standard mouse husbandry); this is a reasonable inference given home-cage testing.
D3 for 2BC scored 15+ since baseline drinking spanned 2 weeks (Mon-Fri) plus alternating drinking weeks for 4 more weeks plus 5 post-injection sessions — well over 15 recording days.
D2 for 2BC scored 2 (61 min-6 h) as drinking sessions were 2 h.
